clue.text: I will serve as example of good landlord.

definitions.text: I will serve as example of
definitions.meaning: the letter I, printed upright and large, is one instance of an upper-case character
a landlord who lets property well is, punningly, one who lets in a first-rate way

explanation.surface: A person promises to be a model of fine hospitality as an innkeeper.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading splits the phrase: 'capital' is old British slang for excellent, and a 'letter' is someone who lets out property.
explanation.definitionFit: Upper-case characters such as I are what the phrase names, and an excellent property-renter is a splendid 'letter'.

clue.text: Walkabout? Just like our Monarchy

definitions.meaning: a walkabout is a stroll, here a leisurely walk taken for one's health
Britain's monarchy is limited by a constitution, so it is of that kind

explanation.surface: A royal walkabout is being praised as typical of the British crown.
explanation.definitionFit: A health-giving walk is an old name for a daily stroll, and Britain's crown is bound by its fundamental laws.

clue.text: Social gathering for some on Fourth of July ?

definitions.text: Social gathering for some on Fourth of July ?

parts.words: Social gathering for some on Fourth of July ?
parts.note: a celebration held on American Independence Day, with a hint that a political faction is also meant

explanation.surface: Americans gather to celebrate Independence Day.
explanation.definitionFit: A festive get-together is the plain sense, and Americans hold such celebrations on Independence Day.

clue.text: Mad Hatter — Alice almost as histrionic

indicators.note: something mad is crazed and disordered, so the letters that follow are scrambled
almost means the word falls just short, so its final letter is dropped

explanation.surface: Two characters from Lewis Carroll's Wonderland are compared for their showiness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'almost' trims Alice to ALIC; 'Mad' then rearranges HATTER plus ALIC. 'Mad' reads as part of the character's name but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Histrionic behaviour is stagy and overdone, like acting on a stage.

clue.text: Shelter Confederates

definitions.meaning: the sheltered side of something, away from the wind
the Confederate army in the American Civil War was General Robert E. Lee's side

explanation.surface: Southern soldiers in the Civil War seek cover.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is Lee's side: Robert E. Lee commanded the Confederate forces.
explanation.definitionFit: The side away from the wind gives protection, and the Confederate camp was the general's faction.

clue.text: Following, making certain king's escaped

indicators.note: the king has got away, so his letter goes missing from the word

parts.note: making certain means ensuring
R is the abbreviation for rex, king

explanation.surface: A monarch's escape is confirmed in the pursuit that follows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'escaped' takes R (king) out of ENSURING; the 's of 'king's' is 'has'.
explanation.definitionFit: Events that come next in time are subsequent ones.

clue.text: River producing hold-ups for drivers

definitions.meaning: a river of north-east England, through Middlesbrough
golfers' drivers hit balls held up on small pegs

explanation.surface: A river is said to cause traffic jams for motorists.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drivers' suggests motorists and 'hold-ups' traffic delays; really they are golf clubs and the pegs a ball sits on.
explanation.definitionFit: The Tees is a river in north-east England, and golfers set the ball on small pegs before a drive.

clue.text: Control toboggan right up a hill

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the words before are read from the bottom, backwards

parts.note: a luge is a racing toboggan
a tor is a rocky hill, as on Dartmoor

explanation.surface: Someone steers a sledge to the right and up a slope.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'up' turns the sledge and the R together, read bottom to top; a tor is a rocky hill of south-west England such as those on Dartmoor.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that governs flow or speed is a controlling mechanism.

clue.text: Tragic hero's convenient book

parts.note: Tristram, the doomed lover of Isolde in Arthurian legend, with the possessive S
convenient means handy

explanation.surface: A doomed hero carries a handy volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Tristram (also Tristan) is the tragic knight of the Tristram and Isolde legend; the 's supplies an S.
explanation.definitionFit: Laurence Sterne's comic eighteenth-century novel is a famous volume.

clue.text: Inert — apart from smaller end, never changing

indicators.note: end places the smaller word's synonym at the tail of the answer
changing means the letters of the word beside it are reshaped into a new order

parts.note: smaller means less

explanation.surface: Something motionless stays unchanged except for its narrow tip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changing' reshapes the word never; 'end' sends the synonym of smaller to the tail. 'apart from' is a nod to the suffix -less meaning without.
explanation.definitionFit: Lacking any spirit or vigour, someone is listless and unmoving.

clue.text: Counter — productive chap losing head on peak

indicators.note: losing its head means the first letter of the name is cut off

parts.note: Hans Geiger, the physicist who produced the radiation counter named after him

explanation.surface: A man whose work proves counterproductive is beheaded on a mountain.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Counter-productive' not as harmful but as 'counter-producing': Geiger made the counter. 'losing head' drops its G.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss Alpine mountain famous for its north face is a summit in the Bernese Oberland.

clue.text: At Formby's lamp-post in Coventry Street?

indicators.note: in means the answer lies inside the run of letters of the two words

explanation.surface: George Formby leans on a lamp-post in a London street.
explanation.walkthrough: George Formby's song 'Leaning on a Lamp-post' has him waiting there for his girl; Coventry Street is in London's West End.
explanation.definitionFit: Waiting by a lamp-post for a sweetheart is a lovers' secret meeting.

clue.text: One bird's beginning is another's completion

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I

indicators.note: beginning picks out the first letter of the word bird

explanation.surface: A riddle about how one bird's start is where another bird ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' means another bird; the 's after it is a link, 'is'. The answer is a wading bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A wading bird sacred in ancient Egypt is one more feathered species.

clue.text: A record's achieving the heights

parts.note: an LP is a long-playing record, plus the S of the possessive

explanation.surface: Someone's record-breaking feat reaches the summit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'record' looks like a sporting achievement; it is a vinyl LP.
explanation.definitionFit: Europe's great mountain range is a byword for lofty summits.

clue.text: High spirits clergyman comes down on with this book

indicators.note: in a down clue, coming down on means sitting above the other piece, so first

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman
high spirits means elation

explanation.surface: A priest disapproves of exuberance and brandishes a book.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes down on' sounds like a scolding, but in a down clue it puts REV above ELATION.
explanation.definitionFit: The last book of the New Testament is the Apocalypse of St John.

clue.text: Brewer's needed at this stage of afternoon

definitions.text: Brewer's needed at this stage of afternoon

parts.words: Brewer's needed at this stage of afternoon
parts.note: a brewer of beer seems meant, but the brew is a pot of the British afternoon drink

explanation.surface: A brewer is wanted around mid-afternoon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Brewer' suggests a beer maker; the brew is the late-afternoon pot that British households make.
explanation.definitionFit: The late-afternoon pause for a cuppa is when a pot is brewed.

clue.text: Like reflex in arm

definitions.meaning: a reflex happens without conscious thought
an arm is a weapon, here a self-loading pistol or rifle

explanation.surface: A reflex is tested on someone's arm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arm' suggests the limb; it is a firearm.
explanation.definitionFit: Involuntary responses happen by themselves, and a self-reloading gun is a weapon of that name.

clue.text: More the sound of a rasp

indicators.note: the sound of says the answer is spoken like the word that follows

parts.note: a rasp is a coarse file, a grater

explanation.surface: Someone describes the harsh noise of a file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rasp' looks like a noise, but it is a tool, a coarse file.
explanation.definitionFit: Larger in amount or degree is a comparative meaning bigger.

clue.text: A single artist's work it isn't a mixture

indicators.note: the words before are said to be a mixture, a jumble of letters to be reordered

explanation.surface: A painting by one master is declared genuine and not a blend of hands.
explanation.walkthrough: The paintings of the Venetian Renaissance painter are named after him in the plural.
explanation.definitionFit: Canvases by the Venetian master are known by his name, so they are one painter's output.

clue.text: It opens in theatre in maybe 50 places

indicators.note: the second in places one letter within the rearranged word
maybe suggests a possible arrangement, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: L is the Roman numeral for 50

explanation.surface: A show opens in theatres in around fifty venues.
explanation.walkthrough: 'maybe' rearranges PLACES to SCAPEL; the second 'in' puts L (50) inside. 'theatre' means an operating theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: A surgeon's knife cuts open the patient in an operating room.

clue.text: Bit of Maths confuses me other parts, too

indicators.note: parts suggests breaking a word apart and putting its letters back in another order
confuses means the letters of the short word are mixed up

explanation.surface: A student finds a piece of mathematics baffling, along with other topics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'parts' rearranges OTHER to THEOR and 'confuses' ME to EM; 'too' links.
explanation.definitionFit: A proposition proved from axioms is a basic unit of mathematics.

clue.text: Start of Times anagram, but not a Chinese puzzle

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the newspaper's name
but not means one letter is left out of the word before

explanation.surface: A newspaper's anagram turns out not to be an oriental puzzle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'but not a' removes just one of the word's three As, so the deletion is a single letter, not every A.
explanation.definitionFit: A dissection puzzle of seven flat shapes rearranged into figures comes from China.

clue.text: Some sort of resistance in Royalist cause ?

definitions.meaning: electrical resistance is measured in these units
abbreviation stamped on British official mail: On Her Majesty's Service

explanation.surface: A rebellion is fought in support of the crown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'resistance' looks military but is electrical; British government letters were franked with the Crown initials.
explanation.definitionFit: Electrical opposition is counted in units named after Georg Ohm, and crown business bore its service initials.

clue.text: Murderer one jailed

annotationWithheld.why: Murderer one jailed (4): the only parse puts I (one) inside CAN, but 'jailed' would have to be both the container indicator and the word giving CAN (jail), a word doing two jobs.

clue.text: Imitative of Gibbon ?

definitions.meaning: a gibbon is an ape, so like or of an ape

explanation.surface: Someone writes in the style of the historian Edward Gibbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gibbon' suggests the historian Edward Gibbon; it is the ape.
explanation.definitionFit: Copying behaviour is monkey-like mimicry, and a gibbon is a primate of that kind.

clue.text: One's taken on vulgar business with a resort in Med

parts.note: one is the Roman numeral I; the 's means has
biz is slang for business

explanation.surface: A person takes on a crude trade at a Mediterranean holiday spot.
explanation.walkthrough: One's = one has, so I has taken on BIZ and A.
explanation.definitionFit: The Balearic island famed for clubbing is a Mediterranean holiday destination.

clue.text: West Ham needing one as a substitute ? Fancy!

indicators.note: one comes on as a substitute, taking the place of a letter in the team's name

parts.note: ham taken as written
one is the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: A London football club needs a substitute player.
explanation.walkthrough: West Ham is a London football club; I comes on for the A in W HAM.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden fancy is a passing impulse or caprice.

clue.text: This sort of bone always starts hurting

indicators.note: starts picks out the first letter of the word always

parts.note: hurting, as an irritating sore patch, means itching

explanation.surface: A certain bone is always the first thing to ache.
explanation.walkthrough: The aitchbone is a cut of beef from the rump.
explanation.definitionFit: The rump bone of beef carries this prefix in its name.

clue.text: Henry IV's beginning to get into trouble, causing split-up

parts.note: Shakespeare's Henry IV opens with Part I

indicators.note: trouble means the short word is stirred up, its letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A king starts getting into difficulties that cause a rift.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beginning' looks like the start of the king's reign, but it is Part I of Shakespeare's two-part play; 'trouble' rearranges INTO to TION.
explanation.definitionFit: Dividing something into sections is a separation or division.

clue.text: Like praise freely given

definitions.meaning: flattering, in the manner of a compliment
given free of charge, as a gift

explanation.surface: Praise is handed out without charge.
explanation.definitionFit: Flattering remarks are admiring ones, and a free ticket is a gratis one.
